title: Federal Open Market Committee reaffirms its "Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy"
summary: The FOMC unanimously reaffirmed its existing Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy at its annual organizational meeting on January 26, 2021. The reaffirmed statement is identical to the framework adopted in August 2020 following the Fed's comprehensive review that included public Fed Listens events. The Committee first adopted a framework statement in 2012.
key_points: FOMC unanimously reaffirmed its existing monetary policy framework at the annual organizational meeting
The reaffirmed statement is identical to the August 2020 statement adopted after the strategy review
The review process included numerous public Fed Listens events around the country
The Committee first adopted a formal framework statement in 2012
This is a continuity statement confirming existing policy framework, not announcing new policy
why_it_matters: This press release confirms that the Fed is maintaining the flexible average inflation targeting framework adopted in August 2020. For market participants, this signals continuity in the Fed's reaction function rather than any policy shift. The framework emphasizes a 2% inflation target and maximum employment as longer-run goals, with the Fed willing to allow inflation moderately above 2% for some time following periods when it was below 2%.
macro_context: The reaffirmation maintains the August 2020 framework framework where the Fed seeks to achieve inflation moderately above 2% for some time to achieve an average of 2% over time, and will use all available tools to promote maximum employment. This framework was developed during the Fed's 2019-2020 comprehensive review of monetary policy strategy, tools, and communication practices.
